claim: game.ts is a merge-conflict hotspot that cannot be tested
statement: src/game.ts is a 2874-line hub touched by 53 of the 172 commits on main, and most feature commits also edit it. Two of the figures and the reason given are wrong. It has 112 import statements carrying about 200 symbols, not about 120. Callback wirings count about 50 to 75 depending on method, not exactly 67. Pixi does not stop it loading in Node: once engine/audio is mocked, game.ts imports fine. What fails is building it: `new Game(...)` throws `document is not defined`, and update() and startStock() are private, so no Node test reaches its logic.
evidence: wc -l src/game.ts = 2874. `git log --oneline main -- src/game.ts | wc -l` = 53 of 172 (47 of 138 without merges). Scratch count-imports.mjs: 112 import statements, 200 symbols. `grep -noE "\b(on[A-Z]\w*)\s*(:|=)[^=]"` = 50. Commits touching each area that also touched game.ts: world 25/31, sim 41/57, ui 38/43, render 24/40. Scratch vitest runs: game-mocked.scratch.test.ts (only engine/audio mocked) imports game.ts with no error; audio-import.scratch.test.ts (no mock) gives `ReferenceError: document is not defined`; game-construct.scratch.test.ts `new Game(spec)` gives the same error (constructor game.ts:383 calls document.getElementById, and the field initialisers create DOM objects).
proposedFix: Make engine/audio free of side effects at import, then move update()'s simulation body and startStock out into a src/sim module that game.ts calls, so feature branches stop editing the hub.
acceptance: A vitest under src/ imports src/game.ts with no vi.mock and passes (today it fails with ReferenceError: document is not defined). The extracted per-tick step has its own Node test in src/sim.

claim: Gameplay rules hidden in the hub
statement: Gameplay rules live only in Game.update and the module-private startStock() in src/game.ts, and no test covers them. They are: the tick order; famine halving station production (0.5) and slowing trains (0.7); a passenger catchment of finished houses within Chebyshev distance 7; and one ticket per day when at least one contract was completed that day. The catchment rebuilds an array of every house for each passenger station on every unpaused 20 Hz tick. The famine 0.5 for buildings lives separately, in sim/buildings.ts.
evidence: src/game.ts: update() runs 1974-2037 (cited as 1982). famineMul 0.5 at 1998, `famine ? 0.7` at 2019. Catchment at 2000-2005 (`<= 7` at 2003, only for def.id==='station'). Daily ticket at 2028-2035. startStock() at 155-174, used at 413. The buildings' own famine 0.5 is at sim/buildings.ts:53 and :90. `grep -rn "startStock\|famineMul\|completedToday" src` finds no test of these rules, and no test imports game.ts.
proposedFix: Move the gdt>0 body of Game.update and startStock() into a src/sim module with named constants, keeping the order and values unchanged, and have game.ts call it.
acceptance: A src/sim test asserts: famine halves station ticks and multiplies fleet speed by 0.7; the catchment counts only houses with progress>=1 within Chebyshev radius 7; exactly one ticket per day with completedToday>0; startStock matches the track-cost formula. `grep -n "famine ? 0\|<= 7" src/game.ts` returns nothing.

claim: Sim dt scales with game speed, no sub-stepping
statement: The game loop always steps at SIM_HZ=20 (0.05 s), and GameClock.advance multiplies that step by the speed, so at 3x each fleet.tick gets gdt=0.15 s. There is no sub-stepping in Game.update, Fleet.tick or Train.tick, and occupancy is rebuilt only per tick. Over the same game time, results measurably differ by speed: arrival times, stopping positions and blockedTime all change.
evidence: sim/time.ts:41 `const dt = realDt * this.speed`. engine/loop.ts:31-35 fixed stepMs. game.ts:155 area SIM_HZ=20, update() at 1981 `clock.advance(dt)`, fleet.tick at 2020. fleet.ts:879-881 rebuildOccupancy once at the start of each tick (and again at 895). Scratch speed-dt.scratch.test.ts runs 180 game-s on one line at gdt 0.05 vs 0.15. 1 train: arrivals 39.35/110.20/161.15 vs 39.15/109.95/160.80. 2 trains: blockedTime 9.55 vs 10.2. 3 trains: the held train stops at dist 68.069 vs 68.685, blockedTime 21.2 vs 19.2 and 14 vs 18.9.
proposedFix: Advance the sim in fixed 0.05 s game-time sub-steps, running clock.speed steps per loop tick instead of one scaled step, so results do not depend on game speed.
acceptance: A Node test runs the same Fleet scenario for 180 game-seconds at 1x and through the 3x stepping path, and gets identical arrival times, train distances and blockedTime (today 39.35 vs 39.15 s and 9.55 vs 10.2 s).

claim: Audio import side effects force mocks in every sim test, with inconsistent shapes
statement: Importing src/engine/audio touches document and window, so every test that loads trains, fleet, build, houses or ui/dom at runtime must vi.mock it. Six tests do, but not every sim test: body, compat, lineSpeed, save and traffic do not need to. recovery.test.ts mocks sfx as an object `{ play: vi.fn() }`, while the real export is a function. Calling sfx under that mock throws TypeError. Nothing in recovery.test reaches an sfx call today, so this trap is latent. The cited line numbers do not exist: the files are 173 and 80 lines long.
evidence: src/engine/audio.ts:39 `private ambience = new Ambience()`, 57-61 window.addEventListener in the constructor, 170 `export const audio = new AudioBus()` at module load. src/engine/ambience.ts:10 document.addEventListener in the constructor. vi.mock('../engine/audio') appears in reclassStroke, narrowDepot, recovery, reclass, expansion and switchForms tests. recovery.test.ts:10 `{ sfx: { play: vi.fn() } }`. sfx is called at trains.ts:1942, 1958 and 2218. Scratch audio-import.scratch.test.ts: an unmocked import gives `ReferenceError: document is not defined`. Scratch recovery-mock.scratch.test.ts: under that mock `sfx('train.arrive')` throws TypeError.
proposedFix: Register the window and document listeners in AudioBus and Ambience lazily (on first update or unlock, guarded by typeof window), and change recovery.test.ts:10 to `{ sfx: vi.fn() }`.
acceptance: A Node test imports src/engine/audio without vi.mock and passes (today: ReferenceError: document is not defined). `grep -rn "sfx: { play" src` returns nothing.

claim: CI does not run on develop or agent branches
statement: On main and on origin/develop, ci.yml runs on push to main only, plus pull_request. This branch adds develop to push.branches, but develop runs the copy of ci.yml on develop itself, so push CI on develop starts only after this change is merged there. Agent branches still get no CI when pushed, but every pull request from them (into develop) does run CI, so the validation path is covered.
evidence: `git show main:.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `git show origin/develop:.github/workflows/ci.yml` have push.branches [main]. HEAD ci.yml:3-6 has push [main, develop] and pull_request. scope.yml runs on pull_request to develop. labels.yml and ref-hygiene.yml run on push to develop/main, path-filtered.
proposedFix: Merge this branch's ci.yml (push on main and develop) into develop and keep pull_request as the CI gate for agent branches.
acceptance: `git show origin/develop:.github/workflows/ci.yml` lists develop under push.branches, and a pull request from an agent branch into develop shows the CI check running.

claim: window.game is an untyped public API
statement: main.ts sets window.game = game for every build, production included. There is no global Window type for it, and the three tracked scratchpad scripts reach into Game members through it, including the private onTrackChanged. Typecheck and lint cover only src, so renaming any of these members passes CI and breaks the scripts only when someone runs them.
evidence: src/main.ts:116 `(window as unknown as { game: Game }).game = game` (not guarded by DEV). No `declare global`/`interface Window` in src. scratchpad/art-sheets.mjs:35-47 uses g.atlas/.keys. art-world-shots.mjs:19-46 uses settings, closeMenus, clock, camera.zoomBy and applySettings. traffic-scenario.js:7-117 uses track, fleet, traffic, regions.unlocked, world.rebuildFog, camera, trainRenderer, app.ticker and g.onTrackChanged (private, game.ts:1173). tsconfig include ["src"]; `tsc --listFilesOnly | grep -c scratchpad` = 0; lint = `eslint src`.
proposedFix: Declare `interface Window { game: Game }` globally, and add the three tracked scratchpad scripts (with // @ts-check) to a typechecked config that npm run typecheck covers, making the members they use public.
acceptance: Renaming Game.camera (or onTrackChanged) makes `npm run typecheck` fail with an error in scratchpad/art-world-shots.mjs (or traffic-scenario.js).

claim: Atlas docs disagree with the loader
statement: atlas.ts accepts `resolution` (1-8; above 1 it samples linear with mipmaps) and `partial`. All six shipped atlas JSONs are partial: five at resolution 4, and rolling.json without one (so 1). docs/mcp-setup.md 6.2 still shows a contract with frames only and says textures are sampled nearest, with no mention of `resolution`; only 6.6 mentions `partial`. Main's CLAUDE.md showed the same frames-only contract but never said nearest. On this branch CLAUDE.md defers to AGENTS.md:111-114, which documents both fields. The nearest advice does hold for the Blender path section 6 describes, because pack-atlas.mjs never writes `resolution`; the resolution-4 atlases come from illustrated-sprites.mjs and bridge-kit.mjs.
evidence: src/engine/atlas.ts:16-18 interface, 72-73 resolution validated 1..8, 90-91 `scaleMode: resolution > 1 ? 'linear' : 'nearest'` and mipmaps, 53 partial layering. public/assets: bridges, icons, props, structures and terrain have partial=true, resolution=4; rolling has partial=true, no resolution. docs/mcp-setup.md:237-250 (frames-only JSON, "sampled with `nearest`" at 245), 268 "nearest-sampled atlas", 303 partial. tools/pack-atlas.mjs:143 writes only {partial, frames}. tools/illustrated-sprites.mjs:391 and bridge-kit.mjs:177 write resolution. `git show main:CLAUDE.md` lines 65-70 show the frames-only contract.
proposedFix: Update docs/mcp-setup.md 6.2 to show the contract as `{ frames, partial?, resolution? }`, and say that resolution>1 samples linear with mipmaps while pack-atlas output (resolution 1) is nearest.
acceptance: docs/mcp-setup.md section 6.2 names `partial` and `resolution` and says when nearest and when linear sampling applies, matching src/engine/atlas.ts:90-91. `grep -n resolution docs/mcp-setup.md` finds it inside 6.2.

claim: Map expansion changes terrain the player may already own
statement: The comment in expandSave ("old tiles come back unchanged") is wrong. When a generated map grows by a ring, terrain, biome, props and about 75% of tile variants change inside the old area. Variant is hashed on local x,y, and the biome majority, lone-tile cleanup, mountain and river passes are clipped at the map edge. On the live path most changed tiles fall in the outer chunk ring: the chunk just bought (nothing is built on it yet) plus unowned chunks. Occasionally the change reaches an interior chunk the player may already have built on. Old fixed-grid saves that main.ts expands on load also have builds in former border chunks, and fixBuiltTiles only patches water, rock and mountain under them.
evidence: Comment is at src/sim/expand.ts:10 (not 11), with the same promise at src/world/mapgen.ts:36-37. Variant uses hash2(x, y, seed) on local coordinates at mapgen.ts:67. Edge-clipped passes: mapgen.ts:156-161, 210, 381, 441-442. Scratch test verify-world/w1.test.ts, 96->160 (origin -32), terrain diffs: 156, 70, 24, 44 for seeds 20260912, 7412, 1, 99 (exact match), all in ring 1; variant diffs 74-75%; prop diffs 34/33/13/17. The live default size is 160->224: 108/123/61/51 terrain diffs, ring 2 only, variant ~75%, including 748-787 of the 1024 tiles in the start chunk. w1b.test.ts: changes reach up to 31 tiles in from the old edge (seed 123456). w1c.test.ts: 1 of 120 seeds (1057) changes 7 interior tiles, water->forest at (125..127,65..67), in chunk (3,2) next to the start chunk. Callers: game.ts:1606-1614 (buyChunk expands in the same call as the purchase), main.ts:96-108 (expands on load), game.ts:1043 fixBuiltTiles.
proposedFix: Hash variant on world coordinates (x+originX, y+originY) in emptyMap, and generate over a fixed off-map margin so the passes clipped at the map edge (biome smoothing, cleanup, mountains, rivers) see the same neighbourhood whatever the map size. The alternative is to correct the expand.ts:10 promise.
acceptance: A test generates seed 20260912 at 160x160 (origin 0) and at 224x224 (origin -32), and asserts that the terrain, biome, variant and per-tile props of the overlapping 160x160 are identical. Today 108 terrain and 19187 variant tiles differ. A weaker version checks at least the inner 3x3 chunks for 120 seeds; today seed 1057 fails it.

claim: Even region counts start with no owned chunk
statement: regionTierMap measures ring distance from the exact grid centre and rounds it. On an even chunk grid (2x2, 4x4, 6x6...) no chunk gets tier 0, so a new game owns nothing. mapgen's start chunk is at floor((n-1)/2) and so lands on tier 1. With no owned chunk nothing is revealed, so nothing can be bought, and ensureDepot finds no unlocked tile. Map sizes 64, 128, 192, 256, 320, 384 and 448 hit this: the mapSize slider allows them, and so do the editor's default level size of 64 and levelForEdit's default of 64 with start tier 0.
evidence: src/world/regions.ts:7-12 (cx=(regionsX-1)/2, Math.round). mapgen.ts:100, 270, 309 use floor((regionsX-1)/2), and so does game.ts:1523 (ensureDepot, which requires isTileUnlocked). Slider: rules.ts:362-368 (min 32, max 480, step 32); sanitize at rules.ts:418 only rounds to a multiple of 32. menu.ts:237 sets size '64'; main.ts:34 defaults size to 64; game.ts:422 calls applyTier only when start.tier > 0. Scratch w2.test.ts: owned@tier0 = 0 for 48, 64, 128, 192 and 256; 1 for 32, 96, 160, 224 and 480; mapgen start chunk tier = 1 on the even grids. w2b.test.ts: 64 gives owned=0, revealed=0, tiers [1,1,1,1]; 128 gives owned=0, revealed=0.
proposedFix: Make regionTierMap use the same integer start chunk as mapgen (floor((n-1)/2)) with an integer Chebyshev distance, or restrict mapSize and editor sizes to odd chunk counts. Either way, existing even-grid saves that persisted an all-false regions array need a decision.
acceptance: For every size s in 32..480 step 32, plus the editor's 32/64/96/128, new RegionState(emptyMap(1,s,s),0).ownedCount() === 1, and the owned index equals floor((regionsY-1)/2)*regionsX + floor((regionsX-1)/2). This fails today for 64, 128, 192, and so on.

claim: Pathfinding ignores class and gauge joints
statement: findPath (and walkBack) only check opensTo on the neighbour. They never apply classesJoin, so a route can cross a regular->narrow or a regular->high_speed joint that has no transition, where TrackGraph.connected() and reach() say the track is not joined. In normal play the build check refuses to lay such a joint. A train's canUse predicate also blocks gauge mixing, but it does not block a regular->high_speed joint without a transition for an in-cab train. Track loaded from saves and levels is placed without the joint check. contractDispatch.legLength and fleet.firstBlockedTile call findPath with no access predicate.
evidence: src/world/pathfinding.ts:53 (opensTo only); walkBack at pathfinding.ts:118. track.ts:359-368 (connected with classesJoin), 374-399 (reach), 174-178 (classesJoin). Build guard: src/sim/build.ts:349-366. Unchecked loads: game.ts:437-441 and game.ts:1091-1094. No access predicate: contractDispatch.ts:187-188 and fleet.ts:227-232. Scratch w3.test.ts: regular (2,1..4) plus narrow (2,5..9) gives connected(2,4,S)=false and reach excludes (2,9), yet findPath returns 9 segments [2,1]..[2,9]. A regular-gauge canUse predicate gives null. Regular plus high_speed with no transition, under an in-cab access predicate, gives a 9-segment path.
proposedFix: In findPath and walkBack, gate each step on track.connected(x, y, out) instead of track.opensTo(nx, ny, nin). This is identical for joints that are valid today and refuses the unjoined ones.
acceptance: New test 1: lay regular straights at (2,1..4) and narrow straights at (2,5..9) with TrackGraph.place; findPath from {2,1,N} to (2,9) is null (today 9 segments). Test 2: the same with high_speed instead of narrow is null. Test 3: regular, then a transition, then high_speed still returns a path.

claim: pathfinding.ts has no unit tests
statement: There is no src/world/pathfinding.test.ts. findPath is called directly only in expansion.test.ts:187-191: one straight line, testing bridge-mass access. That checks only null versus non-null, never the route, its cost, the switch-curve penalty, avoid, tollOf or maxCost. walkBack runs only indirectly through Train.spawnAt in expansion.test.ts and recovery.test.ts and is never asserted itself. MinHeap ordering is untested.
evidence: ls src/world/pathfinding.test.ts: no such file. Direct calls: grep shows findPath only at src/sim/expansion.test.ts:187,191. walkBack is reached via trains.ts:1090 in spawnAt, called at expansion.test.ts:179,208,232,290,315,395 and recovery.test.ts:119. recovery.ts imports only the PathSegment type from pathfinding. No coverage provider is installed (node_modules/@vitest has only mocker and spy).
proposedFix: Add src/world/pathfinding.test.ts covering route choice, reconstruction, the predicates, maxCost, walkBack and heap order.
acceptance: Tests that fail if the code is wrong: (a) through a switch, the cheaper of two routes is chosen, and the curve penalty is +0.2; (b) null when the target is unreachable or beyond maxCost; (c) the start tile is not accepted as the target; (d) for consecutive segments s[i]->s[i+1], s[i+1].in === opposite(s[i].out) and the tiles are adjacent; (e) avoid, access and tollOf change the result; (f) walkBack returns N contiguous segments on a straight and stops at a dead end; (g) the heap pops 1000 random priorities in non-decreasing order.

claim: World imports Simulation, and generateMap reads hidden global state
statement: src/world imports runtime state from sim and data. mapgen imports supplyMode, regions and track import rules, and track imports content, which applies localStorage overrides at module load. generateMap's props depend on the global supply mode through placeOilFields and ensureStartDeposits. level.ts:3 is a type-only import, but mapFromLevel calls placeOilFields, so it has the same hidden dependency. Game sets the mode before it generates (game.ts:381), so no live bug was found, but the output is not a pure function of (seed, params). The golden test runs only in the default 'simple' mode.
evidence: Runtime imports: mapgen.ts:2 (supplyMode), regions.ts:2 (rules), track.ts:2 (content), track.ts:3 (rules); level.ts:3 is `import type`. supplyMode() is read at mapgen.ts:236 and 298. content.ts:416 reads localStorage. sim/supply.ts:16 holds a module-level `let mode`. Scratch w5.test.ts, seed 20260912: at 48x48, simple has 354 props and full has 366 (14 oil), with the same terrain hash 643269639. At 160x160, simple has 3573 and full has 3770 (216 oil). mapgen.test.ts never calls setSupplyMode.
proposedFix: Pass the supply mode into generateMap, placeOilFields, ensureStartDeposits and mapFromLevel as an explicit argument from Game, not inside MapGenParams, which is persisted in saves. Also document (or lint) whether world may import sim and data.
acceptance: A test calls generateMap(SEED, SMALL, 'full') once after setSupplyMode('simple') and once after setSupplyMode('full'), and gets an identical props hash. Optionally, an eslint no-restricted-imports rule (or a grep test) fails if src/world/mapgen.ts imports ../sim at runtime.

claim: Golden map is not representative
statement: The golden map tripwire pins a single configuration: 48x48, a 2x2 chunk grid that is even and has no tier-0 chunk (see world-2), at origin 0, in simple supply mode, with props checked only by count. It does not cover the default 160x160 odd grid, an expanded or offset origin, or full-mode oil fields and deposits. The other tests that generate 96x96 maps (elevation and scatter) pin no hashes.
evidence: src/world/mapgen.test.ts:16-17 (SEED, SMALL 48x48), 35-43 (fnv of terrain, biome and variant; props.size 354), no setSupplyMode anywhere. rules.ts:102 sets mapSize 160. placeOilFields returns early unless supply is full (mapgen.ts:236), and so does ensureStartDeposits (mapgen.ts:298), so changing them cannot trip the test. Scratch w5.test.ts: full mode changes the 48x48 props from 354 to 366 while the golden still passes. elevation.test.ts:8,14 and render/scatter.test.ts:8 use 96x96 with no golden numbers.
proposedFix: Add golden cases to mapgen.test.ts: 160x160 at origin 0, 224x224 at origin -32, and 160x160 in full supply mode (setSupplyMode in before/after hooks). Each pins fnv of terrain, biome and variant plus a hash of per-tile prop content, not a count.
acceptance: The new tripwires pass on the current code. Changing the oil threshold at mapgen.ts:247 (0.9975 to 0.997), or swapping two prop kinds while keeping the count, makes the suite fail; today both changes pass mapgen.test.ts.

claim: Collision and deadlock guarantee not under CI
statement: No test that CI runs checks the end-to-end no-collision / no-jam guarantee. Traffic.overlap() (traffic.ts:378-395) only counts and logs. The one assertion on counters.overlaps is in the Playwright script scratchpad/verify-traffic.mjs:48, and nothing checks counters.deadlocks at all. The fixture can run headless, so closing this gap needs no browser.
evidence: Searching for overlap|deadlock|counters in src/**/*.test.ts and tools/**/*.test.mjs finds only an unrelated hit at tools/pack-atlas.test.mjs:92. vitest.config includes only src/** and tools/**, so scratchpad is never run. The overlap check is called from assign() at traffic.ts:253. I ported scratchpad/traffic-scenario.js to Node (scratch verify-gameplay/world.ts + traffic.test.ts, run with `npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.config.mjs traffic`). Results: count 3 passed, overlaps 0, deadlocks 0, stuck 0, 0.27 s. Count 4 pinned passed, all zero, 0.12 s. Count 12 passed, overlaps 0, deadlocks 0, stuck 2, 0.9 s. Mutation probe (mutation.test.ts, with Traffic.assign turned into a no-op): the pinned case jams for 240 s with stuck 4 and passed=false, yet overlaps stays 0 and deadlocks stays 0. So the test needs to assert passed and stuck as well as the two counters.
proposedFix: Port scratchpad/traffic-scenario.js into src/sim/trafficScenario.test.ts using the expansion.test.ts world fixture with audio mocked. Assert passed===true, overlaps===0, deadlocks===0 for counts 3, 4-pinned and 12, plus stuck===0 for the 3 and 4-pinned cases.
acceptance: `npm test` runs the new file in under 3 s and it passes on the current code. It fails when Traffic.prototype.assign is stubbed to leave claimLimit at Infinity (the pinned case then reports passed=false).

claim: trains.ts and fleet.ts mix several concerns, so parallel agents will collide
statement: trains.ts is 2460 lines and puts consist physics, routing, fuel, loading, contract jobs, retreat/recovery and save in one file, mostly inside one Train class. Two cases are thinner than the claim says: Train applies signals (trains.ts:1652-1670), but the signal model lives in signals.ts; recovery reservations live in recovery.ts. In fleet.ts, chooseNext (634-814) sits next to tick orchestration (879-953). Git history shows parallel agent branches already collided on these two files.
evidence: `wc -l` gives 2460 for trains.ts and 962 for fleet.ts. trains.ts layout: consistPhysics:100, fuel block 818-1063, routing 1208-1420, tick/tickMove 1424-1903, tickLoad:1965, depart:2156, planRetreat/retreat 2243-2320, toJSON/fromJSON 2342-2459. fleet.ts:634 opens chooseNext and its closing brace is at 814; tick runs 879-953. 5 of the 34 merges had both sides editing trains.ts and/or fleet.ts since the merge base: 12f59f7, 9604b74, 345b2ef, 00fb963 and 1fe568f, all worktree-agent branches. docs/process/lifecycle.md:60-72 runs every task without an open Blocked-by in parallel. It has no rule for two same-role tasks writing the same file.
proposedFix: Add a planning rule to lifecycle.md step 3 and the core skill: two tasks that write the same file (in practice src/sim/trains.ts or fleet.ts) are never ready together, and the later one is marked Blocked by the earlier. A later gameplay refactor can split Train's load, fuel and serialization regions out.
acceptance: docs/process/lifecycle.md and .claude/skills/core/SKILL.md state the same-file serialization rule. In a dry-run plan with two gameplay tasks that both name src/sim/trains.ts, only one is labelled status:ready.

claim: Sim outcome depends on game speed
statement: The mechanism is real. Each fixed 20 Hz step advances the sim by gdt = 0.05 x speed game-seconds. Train speed and position use an explicit Euler update. Catenary load is smoothed per tick, not per game-second. Claims are assigned once per tick. Continuous values do drift with game speed. But in the traffic fixture the discrete outcomes (passed, yields, overlaps, deadlocks, stuck, final tiles) were identical at 1x, 2x and 3x. The step is clamped to blockDist, so a larger gdt does not cause overruns.
evidence: time.ts:5 has SPEEDS; advance() at time.ts:40-44 does dt = realDt*speed. game.ts:176 sets SIM_HZ=20. game.ts:1982 computes gdt and game.ts:2020 calls fleet.tick(gdt). Integration is at trains.ts:1785-1793; the clamp to remaining/blockDist is at 1790-1794. catenary.ts:139-145 does load = load*0.7 + acc*0.3 per call. traffic.assign is called once per tick at fleet.ts:884. Scratch speed-save.test.ts (single f7 on a straight line), distance after the same 8.0 game-s: 4.691 at 1x, 4.874 at 2x, 5.058 at 3x (the 3x run covers 8.1 s). First arrival: 46.15 s, 46.0 s, 45.9 s. Catenary load after 1 game-s at a constant 10 u/s: 9.992, 9.718, 9.177. Scratch traffic.test.ts at speeds 1/2/3 for counts 3, 4-pinned and 12 gave identical passed, yields, overlaps=0, deadlocks=0, stuck and heads. Finish times were 19.75/19.6/19.65 s and 116.25/116/115.5 s.
proposedFix: Have Fleet.tick split any gdt larger than 0.05 into fixed 0.05 game-second substeps, so game speed only changes how many steps run per real step.
acceptance: A vitest runs the single-train line and the traffic fixture with fleet.tick(0.15) versus three calls of fleet.tick(0.05). Distance, speed, arrival time and traffic counters match to 1e-9. Today distance after 8 game-s differs: 4.691 vs 5.058.

claim: Save/load is not continuous
statement: Train.fromJSON always sets state 'noRoute' with stateTime 10 (trains.ts:2455-2456). path, holding and blockedTime are not saved. Speed, atStation and yieldCount are also lost, which the claim did not mention. So a moving or loading train stops and re-plans after a load. Traffic stats (lastMoveAt, used for claim priority at traffic.ts:264) and yieldCount (traffic.ts:265) are not in the save at all.
evidence: toJSON (trains.ts:2342-2395) has no speed, state, path, holding, blockedTime or yieldCount. The game.ts:996-1026 save object has no traffic entry. Scratch speed-save.test.ts did a round trip through toJSON, JSON and fromJSON mid-run. Moving train at t=6: state moving->noRoute, speed 1.472->0, hasPath true->false. 24 s later it was 1.27 tiles behind control (35.80 vs 37.07). Loading train at t=47.15: loading->noRoute. 40 s later it was 1.03 tiles off control (98.58 vs 99.61).
proposedFix: Save speed, state/stateTime, the station the train stands at, holding, blockedTime and yieldCount in Train.toJSON. This needs a SAVE_VERSION step whose default reproduces today's noRoute restart. Restore them in fromJSON so only the path is re-planned.
acceptance: A vitest round-trips a moving train and a loading train mid-run. After 30 game-s of fleet.tick each is within 0.01 tile of an uninterrupted control (today 1.27 and 1.03 tiles apart), and save.test.ts's migration registry still passes.

claim: Stale docs would mislead agents

claim: Render and art contract lives in sim/body.ts

claim: A malformed or old content override bricks startup
statement: A content override that is malformed makes validateContent throw instead of returning problems. buildContent has no try/catch and runs at module load, so the whole module graph fails before boot() runs: no menu, no editor and not even the boot error box. The 'old override' half does not hold. Replaying the bundle the editor would have saved at each of 35 data commits since it was added: every pre-38ba5bc snapshot is rejected cleanly and the shipped data is used; every later one is accepted. None of them throws. The editor cannot store a throwing bundle either, because Apply calls validate(), which throws first. So it takes a hand-edited or foreign localStorage value, or a future change to a table's shape.
evidence: src/data/content.ts:441-565 (validateContent iterates b.contracts.templates, b.stations.levels[k] and Object.entries(b.track.pieces) without guards); content.ts:567-580 (buildContent has no try/catch); content.ts:590 (runs at module load); 22 non-test modules import data/content. Probe verify-movement/m1.probe.test.ts: override {contracts:{}} or {locomotives:null} gives 'TypeError: list is not iterable', {stations:{defs:[]}} gives 'reading capacity', {track:{}} gives 'Cannot convert undefined'. Importing src/sim/contracts.ts cascades the same throw. Probe m2hist.probe.test.ts: 35 historical snapshots, 0 throw.
proposedFix: In buildContent, wrap validateContent(merged) in try/catch and treat a throw as a rejected override (warn and return base), and make the per-table checks null-safe.
acceptance: A vitest test stubs localStorage 'terepasztal.content' with {"contracts":{}}, {"locomotives":null}, {"stations":{"defs":[]}} and {"track":{}}, then dynamically imports src/data/content.ts. The import must not throw and content.locomotives must equal DEFAULT_CONTENT.locomotives. Today it throws 'TypeError: list is not iterable'.

claim: Content overrides are unversioned full snapshots
statement: Confirmed: Apply stores the whole draft, which is a clone of every table, with no version stamp, so an accepted override hides later shipped changes to every table. For example, a snapshot saved at 38ba5bc hides the mk48 locomotive shipped since. Also confirmed: a contracts table without rarities, or stations.levels without crew, passes validateContent (it returns []) and then crashes in ContractBoard.rollRarity or in the Station.crew getter. Not confirmed: that stored full snapshots reach that crash. Every real pre-rarities snapshot fails validation for other reasons, such as the missing 'transition' track piece. The crash is reachable through the editor's per-table Import of an old contracts export, or a hand-edited override.
evidence: src/ui/contentScreen.ts:38,45 (draft = clone(content)) and :368 (writeContentOverrides(this.draft)); contentScreen.ts:343-344 (Import merges any key). content.ts:441-565 never checks contracts.rarities or levels.crew. contracts.ts:45 (RARITIES = contractData.rarities) and :115 (RARITIES.filter); stations.ts:109 (LEVELS.crew[...]). Probe m2.probe.test.ts: 5ee6f37^ contracts.json in the current bundle gives validate [], then generate() throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading filter) at rollRarity (contracts.ts:115)'. With crew deleted, validate gives [] and the crew getter throws 'reading 0'. A 38ba5bc locomotives snapshot hides ['mk48'].
proposedFix: Make validateContent require every field the sim reads (contracts.rarities, all eight stations.levels arrays), and have the author choose between per-table diffs and a content-version stamp that discards stale overrides.
acceptance: validateContent(DEFAULT_CONTENT with contracts.rarities deleted) and validateContent(DEFAULT_CONTENT with stations.levels.crew deleted) each return a non-empty list; today both return []. Then, once the author has decided: an override written at an older content version no longer hides an id shipped later, such as mk48.

claim: Contract RNG not persisted
statement: ContractBoard.toJSON leaves out the RNG state, while Gacha, Crafting and Weather store theirs. On load the board is rebuilt with new Rng(seed ^ 0x5eed), so after any load the offer stream restarts from the start of the game. The game then continues differently than it would have without the save and load. One nuance: reloading the same save always gives the same stream, so this makes offers after a load predictable rather than letting a player reroll them by reloading.
evidence: src/sim/contracts.ts:298-306 (toJSON has no rng) and :307-317 (load); game.ts:824; gacha.ts:133,138, crafting.ts:209,228 and weather.ts:93,101 do persist it. Probe m3.probe.test.ts: toJSON keys are [contracts,nextId,nextRefresh,stats,completedToday]. The next 5 offers uninterrupted are ['Local haul|uncommon|4->2|coal|26',...]; after a load they are ['Local haul|common|4->2|wood|19','Bulk order|rare|4->2|wood|110',...], identical to a fresh game's first 5. Reloading twice gives the same stream.
proposedFix: Add rng: this.rng.state to ContractBoard.toJSON and restore it in load when it is a number, the way Crafting.load does, leaving old saves on the reseeded stream.
acceptance: Vitest test: board A with Rng(s) generates 5 offers and is saved with toJSON; board B with Rng(s) loads that save. B's next 5 generate() results must equal A's next 5. Fails today.

claim: Rules keys silently dropped; dead migration write
statement: reputationMul and tradeCycleDays are in Rules and DEFAULT_RULES but not in RULE_META, so sanitize resets them to their defaults on every setRules and readRules. Nothing reads tradeCycleDays: Trade.cycleSeconds() uses weekSeconds(). The migration write is dead, and it also overwrites any value an old save held. Correction: the write is in the from:11 step (v11 to v12), not v10 to v11. reputationMul is already marked @deprecated with no effect, so its reset is harmless.
evidence: src/sim/rules.ts:28,58 (fields), 96,117 (defaults), 411-420 (sanitize copies only RULE_META keys); src/sim/save.ts:276-283 (from:11 sets j.rules.tradeCycleDays = 7); src/sim/trade.ts:68-70 (cycleSeconds returns weekSeconds()). The only grep hits for tradeCycleDays are rules.ts, save.ts and save.test.ts. Probe m45.probe.test.ts: keys missing from RULE_META are ['reputationMul','tradeCycleDays']; setRules({tradeCycleDays:14, reputationMul:3}) leaves 7 and 1; migrating a v11 save with tradeCycleDays:30 gives 7.
proposedFix: Either delete tradeCycleDays and reputationMul from Rules and drop the j.rules.tradeCycleDays write, or wire tradeCycleDays into Trade.cycleSeconds and add it to RULE_META; the author picks which.

claim: Loading a save rewrites global tuning
statement: applySave calls setRules(j.rules) with persist left at its default of true. The save's tuning is merged over the live rules and written to the global 'terepasztal.rules' localStorage key. Rules the save lacks keep the previous session's values; a save with no rules at all keeps them all. Starting a new game reloads the page and reads those stored rules, so the loaded save's tuning carries into the new game. The main menu shows a 'custom rules' marker via rulesDiffer (game.ts:491), so the change is visible but not undone. README says only that tuning is 'stored with the save', so whether loading should change global tuning is unclear.
evidence: src/game.ts:1076 (if (j.rules) setRules(j.rules)); src/sim/rules.ts:440-447 (Object.assign(rules, sanitize({...rules, ...patch})), then localStorage.setItem when persist); rules.ts:421-435 (readRules at module load). No reset on the new-game path: main.ts:71-76 and game.ts newGame then setIntentAndReload. Probe m45.probe.test.ts: stored {trainSpeedMul:2}, then loading a save with {payoutMul:3} gives live {trainSpeedMul:2, payoutMul:3}. After a module reload (the new game), {trainSpeedMul:2, payoutMul:3}.
proposedFix: On load, apply the save's rules in-session only as setRules({...DEFAULT_RULES, ...j.rules}, false), and leave global tuning for the tuning screen to persist.
acceptance: Test through an extracted load-rules helper. Stored rules {trainSpeedMul:2}; load a save with rules {payoutMul:3}. The live rules must have trainSpeedMul at its default and payoutMul 3, and after a module reset rules.payoutMul must be the stored or default value, not 3. Today it is 3.

claim: Save shape assembled outside the domain and untestable
statement: The save shape is built and consumed only in game.ts: startStock at 155-174, snapshot() at 986-1028 and applySave() at 1071-1141. game.ts imports pixi.js and touches document at module load, so node tests cannot import it. The KNOWN_SAVE_KEYS test only checks the 13 keys of oldestSave(). Of the 28 keys snapshot() writes, 15 are never checked by any test. Today all 28 are in KNOWN_SAVE_KEYS, so this is a coverage gap, not a live bug. A snapshot key added without registering would go into saveExtra on load, and nothing would catch it.

claim: Migration logic split and the rule broken
statement: The no-op steps are from:4, 5, 6 and 7, not 9: the from:9 step fills crafting recipes. Their notes describe defaults that load code applies: game.ts:1078 (seasonOffset), 1084-1085 (regions; where there are none it unlocks every chunk the tier allows, not just the start chunk as the step 4 note says), 1135 (ensureDepot), stations.ts:329 (rot ?? 0). Parts of the from:8 and from:9 notes are also done by load code: legacySupplyPending at game.ts:1103, loco modes at trains.ts:671, battery start at trains.ts:2443. claim: Loads crash on content ids that no longer exist
statement: stationDef, buildingDef, locoDef and wagonDef throw on an unknown id. A save that references a removed content id therefore crashes the load: fixBuiltTiles calls stationFootprint and buildingDef, then Station.fromJSON and Train.fromJSON run. Ids that real saves can hold were removed in e28519e (2026-09-06, while saves were v3), for example stations mill and refinery and locos puffer and mogul, and SAVE_MIN_VERSION = 1 still accepts those saves. A content override that hides an id has the same effect. Inventory.load copies items unfiltered, while Crafting.load drops unknown recipe ids.
evidence: src/sim/stations.ts:14-18 (throw at 16); src/sim/buildings.ts:7-11 (throw at 9); src/gacha/items.ts:11-26 (throws at 13 and 18, itemDef at 24); src/gacha/inventory.ts:66-69; src/gacha/crafting.ts:212-229 (known() filter); game.ts:1042-1066 (fixBuiltTiles), trains.ts:2397-2411. Probe m8.probe.test.ts: Station.fromJSON(mill) and stationFootprint(mill) throw 'unknown station mill', buildingDef throws, itemDef(puffer) throws 'unknown wagon puffer', Inventory.load keeps ['puffer'], Crafting.load keeps only ['rocket']. Script removed-ids.mjs lists 17 ids removed over the history.

claim: Import overwrites the real save with near-empty JSON
statement: parseSave checks only that seed is a number and then migrates. importSave writes the result over the real save and reloads. It does not call applySave itself: the next boot's readSave → applySave reads j.clock.time and throws, and because the bad save is now stored, every boot ends on the error box and never reaches the menu. One nuance: a bare {"seed":1} is rejected, because migrations for v11 and v12 happen to throw on missing stations or track. {"seed":1,"version":13}, a version-99 file, or an old version that carries stations and track gets through.
evidence: src/sim/save.ts:357-362 (parseSave); src/game.ts:1726-1739 (importSave: parseSave, writeSettings, then writeSave(j) at 1731 and reload); game.ts:1079 (this.clock.time = j.clock.time); main.ts:85-119 (readSave, then game.applySave) and 136-144 (catch only prints the stack). Probe m9.probe.test.ts: {"seed":1} rejected ('j.stations is not iterable'), version 12 rejected, while {"seed":1,"version":13}, version 99 and {seed,version:5,stations:[],track:[]} are written over the real save with no clock.
proposedFix: Make parseSave return null unless the required v1 fields (clock, economy, track, stations, trains, camera and lastDay) have the right types, so importSave refuses before writeSave and readSave ignores a corrupt stored save.
acceptance: save.test.ts: parseSave('{"seed":1,"version":13}') and parseSave('{"seed":1,"version":99}') return null, while parseSave(JSON.stringify(oldestSave())) still migrates. Today both near-empty inputs come back as objects whose clock is undefined.

claim: Trains are vertically stretched or squashed on inclines on main
statement: Trains stretch and squash on ramps on main and on develop, whose src/render is the same. TrainRenderer.pose passes the rail grade along the train's heading into standOnGround. Its q = 1 + (sgx+sgy)/32 scales the sprite's local y, which on an upright body is its height. Terrace rails climb at most 1 level per tile, and one level is TILE_SIDE_PX/4 = 9.80 px. At that grade a 30 px body draws 20.8 px tall on a ramp rising toward +x and 39.2 px on a falling one, about ±30.6%. The fix (4ae3045, pitchShear/pitchOnRail plus slope.test.ts) is on origin/claude/train-slope-pitch and is in neither develop nor main.
evidence: slope.ts:33-35 (p, q, matrix.set); trainRenderer.ts:155-164 (pose projects the slope onto the heading and calls standOnGround); worldRenderer.ts:1003-1016 railAt grade; terrainRelief.ts:55 step. Scratch verify-uiux/uiux1.test.ts: lineSpans max grade is 0.997-1.000 levels/tile; a 30px body comes out 20.81px at grade +1 and 39.19px at grade -1, the same for heading 0 and pi. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4ae3045 origin/develop` and the same against origin/main both return 1. merge-tree with develop shows no conflict (the branch is 1 commit ahead and 35 behind). The branch's own pitchShear tests pass in scratch (uiux1b.test.ts, 4/4).
proposedFix: Bring 4ae3045's pitchShear/pitchOnRail and its slope.test.ts into develop on a rendering branch, leaving out its scratchpad/slope-pitch files, which are outside the rendering scope.
acceptance: A test in src/render/slope.test.ts poses a sprite for heading 0 and pi/2 on rail grade +1 and -1 level/tile and asserts that local (0,-30) stays 30 px above local (0,0) on screen. It fails today with 20.8 and 39.2.

claim: Build legality depends on the renderer's worker health
statement: WorldRenderer.groundAllows returns true whenever landscape.failed is set, and game.ts wires it in as Builder.groundCheck. A client whose landscape workers fail to start or report an error therefore accepts curves, switches, stations, buildings and decor on bank tiles that a healthy client rejects. The terrace relief that decides this is built synchronously on the main thread, so the check never needed the workers. The rule itself (terrainRelief.groundAllows) lives in src/render.
evidence: worldRenderer.ts:1096-1097 (`return this.landscape.failed || ...`); game.ts:778; build.ts:341,350,507,611,687; landscape.ts:84 (buildRelief runs in the constructor), 85-104 and 216 (fail() on a Worker error or throw); terrainRelief.ts:462. Scratch uiux2.test.ts: under node there is no Worker, so a real Landscape comes up with failed=true. On generateMap(1234), all 1854 land tiles that Landscape.groundAllows(...,'level') rejects pass WorldRenderer.prototype.groundAllows. With failed=false the same tile is rejected.
proposedFix: Remove `this.landscape.failed ||` from WorldRenderer.groundAllows so the main-thread relief always decides; later, move the rule out of src/render into src/world.
acceptance: A headless test builds a Landscape with no Worker (failed=true) and asserts WorldRenderer.prototype.groundAllows(x,y,'level') equals landscape.groundAllows(x,y,'level') for every tile of a generated map. Today 1854 tiles differ on seed 1234.

claim: Mirror and bogie-order logic is duplicated, and unmerged branches collide with it
statement: The duplication is real. The rule that picks a drawn facing and mirrors it is written three times, and the rule that reverses bogie styles is written twice; no test ties the preview to the renderer. The branch part is overstated. origin/art/rear-views-v1, origin/local/train-models and origin/locomotive-render-v1 all carry the same two commits (d333295, 646bda0), not three separate rewrites. Together those commits change body.ts by +92/-17 and trainRenderer.ts by one line, and both files merge into develop without conflict. They do add a third copy of the back-to-front rule in poseSegment. The real conflicts are in rolling atlas files, RESUME.md, src/ui/spritePreview.ts and tools/asset-pipeline/CLAUDE.md. PR #21 (local/train-models) is still open against an old base.
evidence: trainRenderer.ts:145-151; previewLayers.ts:30-33; game.ts:330-337; bogie rule at trainRenderer.ts:288-290 (`back = t.reversed !== seg.mirror`) vs previewLayers.ts:45-46 (`s.mirror ? n-1-k : k`); the reversed flip also sits in sim/trains.ts:1204-1205. On the branches: `git diff 8a11a99 <branch> --stat` gives body.ts 109 lines and trainRenderer.ts 2 lines, 93+/18- in total, with an identical body.ts diff hash on all three. `git log` shows the same two commits on each. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/develop <branch>` auto-merges body.ts and trainRenderer.ts. The only test in previewLayers.test.ts covers narrow-gauge frames.
proposedFix: Add one helper to src/sim/body.ts, next to DRAWN_FACINGS and mirrorFacing, that returns {facing, flip} for an angle and the bogie style index for (k, n, back), and call it from trainRenderer, previewLayers and game.ts.
acceptance: A test asserts that previewLayers' bogie styles and flips for every facing of a mirrored Garratt equal what the shared helper gives with reversed=false, and grep finds `DRAWN_FACINGS.has` only inside body.ts.

claim: Depth-layer contract split across domains
statement: Depth layers are bare numbers scattered across two roles. Render uses 2, 10, 14, 15 and 16. game.ts passes 12, 13, 14, 20, 30, 35, 36, 45 and 46 to setStructure, which defaults to 20. Because depthKey = (x+y)*100 + layer, a layer is worth layer/100 of a tile: a body (15) at x+y = 10.06 sorts at 1021, ahead of a structure (20) on tile x+y = 10 at 1020. There is no named table. The 'no test' half is overstated: iso.test.ts checks that layers break ties and stay below the next tile row. Nothing tests the layer table itself or fractional positions. Layer 14 is shared by bogies and power lines, but bogies overwrite it with s.zIndex-1. Layer 16 is shared by wagon loads and people.
proposedFix: Export a named depth-layer table from src/engine/iso.ts and use its names in place of the literals in src/render and game.ts.
acceptance: A test in iso.test.ts asserts that every table entry is in [0,100) and that the order is bridge rail < train body < marker. A grep for numeric layer arguments to depthKey(...) and setStructure(...) outside iso.ts finds nothing.

claim: Stale docs would mislead a scoped agent

claim: No enforced import boundaries
statement: Nothing enforces import direction between source areas. eslint.config.js has no no-restricted-imports or import-boundary rule, package.json has no dependency-cruiser or madge, and scope.mjs checks which paths changed, not imports. A scan of every non-type relative import finds exactly one edge running upward into UI: src/render/overviewRenderer.ts:6 imports biomeShade from src/ui/minimap.ts, which imports ./dom at line 5.
evidence: eslint.config.js (its only rules are no-unused-vars and no-non-null-assertion); grep for 'cruiser|boundar|madge|import/no' in package.json finds nothing; scratch verify-uiux/edges.mjs, which lists value imports from sim/world/engine/render/gacha/data into ui/editor/game/main and from sim/world into render, finds only `render -> ui 1 render/overviewRenderer.ts`; minimap.ts:5 `import { el } from './dom'`. Owner per scope.mjs: eslint.config.js is engine.
proposedFix: Move biomeShade out of src/ui/minimap.ts into src/render or src/art, then add a no-restricted-imports rule that forbids src/{engine,world,sim,gacha,data,render} from importing ../ui or ../editor; eslint.config.js is a gate file and needs the author's gate:approved label.

claim: Hardcoded user-facing strings bypass strings.ts with no gate
statement: Many player-facing English strings in src/ui, plus three in src/game.ts, skip STR. Nothing checks for this: the ESLint config has no rule for it, and strings.test.ts only checks wording that is already inside STR. The claim is labelled rendering, but none of these files are in src/render. There are more such strings in sim than cited, e.g. economy.ts:23 'Not enough funds' and the Train lastMessage texts in trains.ts.
evidence: Every cited line still holds a literal. Examples: signalGuide.ts:10-31 (the whole guide), buildingPanel.ts:93/94/114/121, decorPanel.ts:68/96-97/121/130, trainSide.ts:25/75-76, game.ts:1808 'Offer: ...', 1875 'Signals?', 1888-1889 the refuel toasts. git blame: almost all cited lines come from 38ba5bc (Codex). The exceptions are namePrompt (3c3d68e), rosterScreen:226 (f038e7d), buildInfo:111 (56d9a4c), townPanel 2 lines (348ada2), vehiclePreview 1 line (9a682e6) and game.ts:1808 (8af811c). eslint.config.js changes only no-unused-vars and no-non-null-assertion. A narrow grep for capitalised literals in text:/btn()/placeholder/aria-label/title/toast in src/ui/*.ts src/game.ts finds 18 hits. That is a lower bound; template strings are not counted.
proposedFix: Move these literals into STR. Add a test in src/strings.test.ts that scans src/ui and src/game.ts and fails when a capitalised literal is passed to text:, btn(), title, placeholder, aria-label or a toast. The 3 strings in game.ts need an Engine edit.
acceptance: The new strings test passes. `grep -nE "(text: ['\`][A-Z][a-z]|btn\(\s*['\`][A-Z][a-z]|placeholder: '[A-Z]|'aria-label': '[A-Z]|title = ['\`][A-Z]|toasts?\.push\(['\`][A-Z])" src/ui/*.ts src/game.ts` finds 0 lines (18 today). Adding `btn('Foo', ...)` to any panel makes the test fail.

claim: Game logic and state mutation live inside DOM panels
statement: Panels do change sim state directly. The market screen's spot buy/sell calls economy.spend/earn and stock.add/take. The gacha screen takes tickets off before gacha.pull. The roster screen sets it.inCab = true; the money for it goes through a game.ts callback. The spot-price formula exists only in marketScreen.ts. The divergence claim is wrong, though: DEAL_BONUS is by design the better rate for standing deals only, and the same screen shows those deal prices from TradeDesk. The 'cannot be tested in Node' part is true: these modules cannot even be imported in Node. All cited files are src/ui, not src/render.
evidence: marketScreen.ts:57-58 (spot formula); 64-70 (spend + stock.add); 81-84 (stock.take + earn); 153-169 (shows TradeDesk.buyPrice/sellPrice). trade.ts:10-11 says 'Standing deals get a little better rate than one-off spot trades'; buyPrice/sellPrice at 54-67. gachaScreen.ts:195 `this.economy.tickets -= cost`. rosterScreen.ts:207 `it.inCab = true`; spendMoney is wired at game.ts:1779. Scratch test verify-rendering/src/r2.test.ts: coal spot buy 32 vs deal 28.8, spot sell 12 vs deal 13.2. `await import('src/ui/marketScreen')` and `gachaScreen` in the vitest node env both throw 'ReferenceError: document is not defined'.
proposedFix: Add the spot-trade, paid-pull and in-cab-fitting operations to sim (TradeDesk.spotBuy/spotSell with their prices, a ticket-checked pull, Inventory/Fleet.fitInCab). UI/UX then makes the three panels call them.
acceptance: A src/sim node test covers spot buy/sell (storage cap, insufficient money, cent rounding), a paid pull that only deducts tickets when the pull happens, and in-cab fitting. `grep -nE "economy\.(spend|earn)|stock\.(add|take)|tickets -=|inCab = " src/ui/marketScreen.ts src/ui/gachaScreen.ts src/ui/rosterScreen.ts` returns nothing.

claim: No UI-to-sim command layer; the name 'intent' is misleading
statement: It is true that no command layer sits between the UI and sim. game.ts hands live Fleet, Builder, Stockpile, Economy and Train references to the panels, and the panels call their methods or write fields directly. The rest does not hold. intent.ts is documented as boot intents in its own doc comment and in AGENTS.md, so the name is not misleading. The game has no undo or replay feature, so that cost is hypothetical. Validation exists wherever panels go through domain methods such as Builder.upgradeBuilding or Fleet.create.
evidence: intent.ts:3-6 doc comment 'Boot intents...'. AGENTS.md Layout: 'src/intent.ts the boot intents'. game.ts:1636-1915 constructs DepotScreen, TrainScreen(fleet, builder, stock...), MarketScreen(stock, economy...), DecorPanel(builder...) and others. Direct field writes: trainScreen.ts:232 (t.mode), 250 (t.fuelPreference), decorPanel.ts:123 (d.rot), stationPanel.ts:211 (s.name), rosterScreen.ts:207 (it.inCab). `grep -rn undo/replay src` finds nothing outside save.test.ts.
proposedFix: Ask the author whether a sim-side command module is wanted. If yes, route panel mutations through it rather than through field writes; if not, record the decision and close the issue.
acceptance: The author's decision is recorded on the issue. If a command layer is adopted, `grep -nE "\b(t|d|s|it)\.(mode|rot|name|inCab|fuelPreference) = " src/ui/*.ts` returns nothing and each command has a node test.

claim: UI mode switch may skip the Fleet re-plan
statement: trainScreen.ts writes t.mode directly and skips the immediate re-plan that Fleet.create does. A moving train still re-plans at its next departure, so in the normal case the switch is only delayed. A train in noRoute that is switched to Production never re-plans: it keeps retrying its dead scheduled stop. Switching from a roaming mode back to Schedule leaves the one-stop schedule that chooseNext wrote, which gets around the two-stop rule. The Contract mode also has no modeHint string, so the hint line is empty.
evidence: trainScreen.ts:232 `t.mode = m`. The re-plan is at fleet.ts:467-477, and the two-stop rule at 464-465. Departure re-plan for dynamic trains: trains.ts:2181-2207. The noRoute branch (trains.ts:1529-1541) only re-dispatches the old schedule. Scratch test verify-rendering/src/r4.test.ts, run with `npx vitest run --dir <scratch>/verify-rendering r4 --reporter=verbose --silent=false`. (1) Schedule to Production while moving: the route changed from [a, wh] to the stocked quarry at tick 193, on reaching a. (2) noRoute (unreachable first stop) switched to Production: still noRoute after 200 s with route [far, wh], while fleet.chooseNext(t) returns the reachable quarry. (3) Production to Schedule: schedule length stays 1, and the train sat 'loading' at that stop for 1000 s. finishRecording (game.ts:2647-2654) also enforces >=2 stops. strings.ts:874-879 has no modeHint.contract.
proposedFix: Add Fleet.setMode(t, mode). For dynamic modes it re-plans like create does, including from noRoute or idle. On a return to Schedule it keeps or restores a schedule of at least 2 stops (the author decides which). trainScreen then calls it instead of writing t.mode.
acceptance: New src/sim tests pass. A schedule train in noRoute that is set to production through Fleet.setMode targets a reachable producer within one tick. A roaming train set to schedule ends with at least 2 stops, or is refused with a message. trainScreen.ts no longer contains `t.mode =`.

claim: Gameplay threshold duplicated as a magic number
statement: The bridge slow-down threshold, mass above 0.8 of bridge capacity, is written as a bare 0.8 in three places with no shared constant. Two are in sim (the speed factor and the approach braking) and one is in the building panel's text. The 0.5 half-speed factor and the 'half speed above' wording are also hardcoded. The tests rely on the threshold implicitly by setting capacity to mass/0.81.
evidence: trains.ts:895 `if (cap && this.mass > cap * 0.8) factor = Math.min(factor, 0.5)`. trains.ts:1761 `if (limit && this.mass > limit * 0.8)`. buildingPanel.ts:94 `Math.round(bridgeCapacity(b)! * 0.8)`. sim/bridges.ts exports no such constant. expansion.test.ts:183 and 233 use `t.mass / 0.81`. trains.ts:745 has an unrelated 0.8 (loadFactor).
proposedFix: Export the threshold and the half-speed factor as constants from src/sim/bridges.ts. Use them at trains.ts:895 and 1761. UI/UX uses the threshold in buildingPanel.ts:94 and moves the label into STR.
acceptance: `grep -n "\* 0\.8\b" src/sim/trains.ts src/ui/buildingPanel.ts` finds only trains.ts:745 (loadFactor). A src/sim test checks the train slows at threshold + epsilon and not at threshold - epsilon, using the constant.

claim: game.ts is the UI composition root and keymap, shared by every domain
statement: src/game.ts (2874 lines) is the UI composition root and holds most of the keymap, plus a few hardcoded strings. ownership.json assigns it to Engine. 'Any UI change must edit it' is overstated, since a change inside one panel file does not. In practice, though, 44 of the 51 commits that touched src/ui also touched src/game.ts. Under the new scope check, a UI/UX task that adds a panel, hotkey or callback therefore needs an Engine change. It is UI work, not src/render.
evidence: wc -l src/game.ts = 2874. Panels are constructed and wired at game.ts:1636-1915. wasPressed hotkeys at game.ts:2478-2599. Escape, R and Delete are in buildController.ts:113-127. Literals at game.ts:1808, 1875, 1888-1889. tools/agents/ownership.json:39 lists src/game.ts under engine, and uiux owns src/ui/** (line 62). The 44/51 count comes from looping over `git log -- src/ui` and checking each commit's file list for src/game.ts.
proposedFix: Move panel construction and wiring, and the play keymap, into UI/UX-owned modules (e.g. src/ui/panels.ts, src/ui/keymap.ts). game.ts would call them through one narrow interface that passes the domain objects once.
acceptance: A UI/UX branch that adds a new panel and a hotkey passes `node tools/agents/scope.mjs check --role uiux` without touching src/game.ts. The 1636-1915 and 2478-2599 blocks are gone from game.ts.

claim: Two tools write the same public/assets/structures.json
statement: Two tools write public/assets/structures.json and each replaces the whole file. tools/illustrated-sprites.mjs writes the 92 illustrated structures frames at resolution 4. The pipeline's game stage packs structures through tools/pack-atlas.mjs, which writes {partial, frames} with no resolution and only the frames in its art-src folder. Assets.csv row 2 (station_victorian -> structures/station_1) is live (not commented out), so the first full run that has input/station_victorian.png drops 91 illustrated frames, and the one it keeps becomes resolution 1. Running illustrated-sprites afterwards loses the pipeline's frame the same way.
evidence: tools/illustrated-sprites.mjs:385-392 writes <group>.json wholesale with resolution: DENSITY(4). tools/asset-pipeline/assets.csv:2 is uncommented; run.py:210-227 runs export_asset and then export_game.pack, which is export_game.py:156-165 calling pack-atlas. tools/pack-atlas.mjs:143-144: table = {partial, frames}, with no resolution and no merge. Scratch run: I copied public/assets/structures.json (res 4, 92 frames) into scratch/p1/out and ran `node tools/pack-atlas.mjs structures --prefix structures/ --src p1/src --out p1/out` with one station_1.png. The result was {"partial":true,"frames":{"structures/station_1":...}}: 1 frame and no resolution key. src/engine/atlas.ts:72 then defaults it to 1. input/ is gitignored (tools/asset-pipeline/.gitignore), so this is latent until the photo exists.
proposedFix: Make pack-atlas refuse, or merge, when the target <group>.json already holds frames or a resolution that its --src does not supply. The author picks which tool owns structures.json.
acceptance: A tools/pack-atlas.test.mjs case starts from an out dir holding structures.json with resolution 4 and 92 frames, then packs a 1-frame src. pack-atlas either exits non-zero or leaves all 92 frames and resolution 4 in place. Today it writes a 1-frame table with no resolution.

claim: A stale doc is a build input
statement: illustrated-sprites.build() does read docs/art-direction/frame-inventory.json, and the counts are right: 2839 keys there, 3462 from today's generators, 25 removed loco_steam_early_small_yellow_* keys. Only scratchpad/build-art-guide.mjs regenerates it, and that needs Playwright plus a running dev server. The staleness has no effect today: all 207 frames the build targets have the same keys, sizes and anchors in the inventory and in today's generators. The real hazard runs the other way. build-art-guide reads the live atlas, which now includes the illustrated res-4 overrides, so regenerating the inventory would feed illustrated sizes back into the build: townhouse would be 58.75 wide instead of 49.
evidence: tools/illustrated-sprites.mjs:266 readJson('docs/art-direction/frame-inventory.json'). Scratch vitest keys.test.ts mocks pixi and stubs ImageData/canvas, then runs every ATLAS_GROUPS generator: generatorKeys 3462, inventory 2839, 25 inventory keys absent (all rolling/loco_steam_early_small_yellow_body_f*), 691 new keys (track 135, wagons 400, rolling 125, structures 13, bridges 18). scratch/dims.mjs evaluates targets() against both lists: 207 targets each, 0 key/size/anchor differences. scratchpad/build-art-guide.mjs:1-18 takes keys from g.atlas in a Playwright page. src/engine/atlas.ts:52-55 layers partial files over the generator. public/assets/structures.json townhouse w=235 at res 4 (=58.75) against inventory width 49.
proposedFix: Have illustrated-sprites take its target frame list headlessly from the src/art generators (or from a generator-only dump), not from the browser-built doc snapshot.
acceptance: A test asserts that every frame illustrated-sprites targets has the same key, w, h and anchor as the current generator output. It fails if the inventory carries a removed key or override-derived sizes. Today it would flag the 25 removed keys only if they were targeted, which they are not.

claim: Root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md have drifted; the canonical file is inverted in the pipeline folder
statement: This was true before commit 7411401, but that commit is in origin/main, origin/develop and HEAD. Root CLAUDE.md now imports AGENTS.md, and AGENTS.md carries both the 'Art direction lives in…' and 'Music is a file, effects are synthesized' rules and says 'sound effects synthesized'. In the pipeline folder, AGENTS.md is the canonical 116-line guide and CLAUDE.md is a one-line '@AGENTS.md'.
evidence: git show 7411401^:tools/asset-pipeline/AGENTS.md is the old 8-line pointer to CLAUDE.md, and 7411401^:AGENTS.md:50 said 'audio synthesized'. Today, for each of origin/main, origin/develop and HEAD: AGENTS.md has 2 matches for the two rules, CLAUDE.md line 1 is '@AGENTS.md', tools/asset-pipeline/CLAUDE.md is '@AGENTS.md', and tools/asset-pipeline/AGENTS.md is 116 lines. AGENTS.md:85, :88 and :95.
proposedFix: None needed; the organisation commit already made AGENTS.md the single source in both places.
acceptance: On develop, `head -1 CLAUDE.md tools/asset-pipeline/CLAUDE.md` prints '@AGENTS.md' twice, and AGENTS.md contains both rules. Both hold today.

claim: The art regression check depends on manual scripts and an undeclared dependency
statement: AGENTS.md (imported by CLAUDE.md) requires re-running scratchpad/art-sheets.mjs and checking that frame counts and anchors did not move. That script only writes screenshots, through Playwright and a running dev server. Playwright is not declared in package.json and resolves only from global or sibling-repo paths. No test or CI step checks generator frame counts or anchors. scratchpad holds 462 tracked files (151 MB tracked; du -sh 146M).
evidence: AGENTS.md:92. scratchpad/art-sheets.mjs:65 is page screenshots only, with no count or anchor output. scratchpad/runtime.mjs:3-22: candidate list (PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE, 'playwright', /opt/node22/..., ../../terepasztal-scratch/...), throw at 22. `grep playwright package.json` finds nothing, and from the repo `import('playwright')` gives ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only typecheck/lint/test/build/prettier. `git ls-files scratchpad | wc -l` = 462. The scratch vitest keys.test.ts enumerated all 3462 generator keys and anchors headless in about 3 s, so a test is feasible. Track dimensions need a real canvas, because trackIllustrated draws with 2D context calls.
proposedFix: Add a headless vitest that snapshots each generator group's frame keys and anchors, so counts and anchors are checked automatically. Leave art-sheets for visual review. Declaring Playwright, which touches package.json, a gate file, is the author's call.
acceptance: `npm test` fails when a generator change adds, removes or re-anchors a frame without updating the snapshot. Today nothing fails.

claim: Content changes break Art tests
statement: tools/building-kit.test.mjs hard-codes 27 families and 560 pictures, but loadInventory derives both from src/data (stations, stations_full, buildings, buildings_full, decor). Any content edit that adds or removes a building therefore fails this Art test.
evidence: tools/building-kit.test.mjs:22-29 has toHaveLength(27), pictures toHaveLength(560) and Set size 27. tools/building-kit.mjs:92-147 reads src/data/*.json. Scratch: I copied src/data to scratch/p5 and pushed one extra entry into buildings.json. loadInventory gave 27/560 for the repo and 28/584 for the copy, so the test's assertions would fail.
proposedFix: Assert the invariant: family count equals the qualifying src/data entries, and pictures equals the sum of ages times 4 rotations. Keep the fixed counts only as a separate, clearly labelled snapshot, or drop them.
acceptance: Adding a building to src/data/buildings.json in a temp copy leaves building-kit.test.mjs green, while breaking the ages times rotations relation still fails it.

claim: The building package and the game disagree on ages and rotations
statement: The facts hold. building-kit has 6 AGES and 4 ROTATIONS keyed structures/<f>_a<age>_r<rot>. The game asks for _r${rot % 2}, and only for multi-tile or long stations; nothing in src asks for an _a<age> key. src/data/ages.json has 3 ages, and art-direction README:13-15 calls nuclear, maglev and hyperloop future concepts. But the gap is a planned staged rollout, not drift. The 2026-10-02 spec says the package fixes conventions 'the game will rely on' and puts the new ages in sub-project 3 (branch buildings/ages-upgrading exists) and four-step rotation in sub-project 4. The concrete defect is that the art-direction README contradicts that later decision.
evidence: tools/building-kit.mjs:11-18 and :80-82. src/ui/buildController.ts:369 and src/game.ts:1464,1475 use _r${rot % 2}. Grepping src for '_a${' finds no consumer. src/data/ages.json: steam/diesel/electric. docs/art-direction/README.md:13-15. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-building-eras-art-package-design.md:17-28 and :73 ('Frame key the game will ask for'). origin/buildings/ages-upgrading is 2 ahead of main.
proposedFix: Update art-direction README:13-15 to point at the 2026-10-02 spec as the current decision on ages and rotations. Leave the game-side integration to sub-projects 3 and 4.
acceptance: docs/art-direction/README.md no longer calls nuclear or maglev 'not existing asset requirements', and links to the building-eras spec.

claim: Pipeline docs contradict the runtime
statement: docs/mcp-setup.md §6 is out of date with the runtime. §6.1 says public/assets 'does not exist yet' (it holds 7 groups) and lists groups without bridges. §6.2 says textures are sampled with nearest and not to upscale, but atlas.ts accepts resolution 1-8 and samples res>1 linearly with mipmaps. The contract shown omits partial and resolution. art-direction README:3 links to scratchpad/illustrated-hd/README.md, which does not exist and has no git history; scratchpad/illustrated/README.md exists. Separately, AGENTS.md says pack-atlas writes resolution?, but pack-atlas never emits it.
evidence: docs/mcp-setup.md:231 ('it does not exist yet'), :234-235 (group list without bridges; src/art/index.ts:15-28 includes bridges), :245 ('nearest… do not upscale'). src/engine/atlas.ts:72-73 (resolution 1..8), :87-92 (scaleMode linear when resolution>1). `ls public/assets` lists bridges/icons/props/rolling/structures/terrain/terrain-surfaces. `ls scratchpad/illustrated-hd` gives no such directory, and `git log --all -- scratchpad/illustrated-hd/README.md` is empty. tools/pack-atlas.mjs:143.
proposedFix: Rewrite mcp-setup §6.1-6.2 for today's contract (existing public/assets, bridges group, partial, resolution with linear sampling) and fix the README:3 link to scratchpad/illustrated/README.md.
acceptance: A doc-link check (like tools/building-docs.test.mjs) finds no dead relative links in docs/art-direction/README.md and docs/mcp-setup.md. §6 mentions partial, resolution and bridges.

statement: Three old art branches are unmerged and 67 commits behind main, with very large diffs from their merge base: art/rear-views-v1 (14 ahead, 1144 files), local/train-models (15 ahead, 1337 files) and locomotive-render-v1 (13 ahead, 1097 files). All last changed 2026-09-27, and most of the changed files are scratchpad/train-models renders plus art-src/rolling, art-src/wagons and assets/source. buildings/art-package is 39 ahead and 8 behind, last changed 2026-10-08.

Last commits 2026-09-27 10:58/13:01/09:44 -0400. None is an ancestor of origin/main. Merge base 8a11a99 (2026-09-26).
